plan.name: Explain TypeScript acceptance refusals
plan.summary: For Vitest and Jest, make diagnostic refusals from the TypeScript precheck list every diagnostic's TS code, part-relative file and one-based line/column when available, and complete flattened message, including chained messages; explicitly identify diagnostics without a source location, and retain these details in run output, check feedback and the factory's refusal comment. Carry the formatted details as authenticated parent diagnostic events with Reason chunks before the refused event, respecting the existing 4096-byte frame limit, and collect them only as refusal detail; preserve diagnostics beyond the current 700-character runner and 40-line comment clipping while retaining the total comment limit, omission notice, marker, closing instructions and local-path sanitization. Keep all attribution, selection, isolation and completion rules unchanged, and extend the existing offline Node fixtures to cover multiple diagnostics, missing modules, unrelated type errors and refused TS2305 cases as well as the unchanged admitted missing-export case. Teach both initial and revised planning prompts, and docs/factory.md, how to test a module the plan creates: use relative imports instead of project path aliases, hold the relative dynamic-import specifier in a string-typed variable, declare the returned API type locally, assert successful loading inside the selected async test so absence produces a completed assertion failure, and then assert the module's behavior, with a short Vitest example and its Jest import equivalent exercised by the offline fixtures. Update SPEC.md's Node acceptance description with existing decision citations (D-0359, D-0122 and D-0294); the merger records the new diagnostic-reporting decision, since the plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestNodeDiagnosticRefusalsReachPlanning788
tests.says: Every authenticated precheck diagnostic survives the native check result and planner feedback for Vitest and Jest, including messages longer than the old runner limit, while the refusal never counts as an acceptance failure.

tests.name: TestTypeScriptNewModulePlanningGuidance788
tests.says: Initial and revised planning instructions explain the unchanged TypeScript attribution boundary and include a locally typed, relative dynamic-import example that asserts loading and behavior inside the selected test.

tests.name: TestNodeDiagnosticRefusalComment788
tests.says: The factory's refusal comment retains all diagnostic lines that fit its existing size limit, including lines after the old forty-line cutoff, while keeping its marker and revise instructions.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and three acceptance tests covering diagnostic reporting and new-module guidance, without changing `repo/`. Check 1 passed: all three tests fail on the base as required, and the resulting change requires a person to merge.
